title: History of Windows, macOS, and Linux

spans.alt: History of Windows, macOS, and Linux
spans.caption: Key steps and ideas

spans.text: Microsoft introduced Windows 1.0 on November 20, 1985. The team led by Bill Gates designed a graphical environment that made windows and mouse input easier on MS-DOS computers; the first release was not a standalone modern kernel. The Windows NT family began in 1993 with a more robust, network-capable base, and modern Windows continues that line.

Apple released the Macintosh on January 24, 1984, aiming to make personal computers approachable through icons, windows, and a mouse. Teams including those led by Jef Raskin and Steve Jobs contributed. Mac OS X, released in 2001, drew on NeXTSTEP and Unix-based Darwin. macOS has Unix roots; Linux is a separate project.

Richard Stallman announced GNU in 1983 to build free Unix-like tools. Linus Torvalds announced work on a new kernel on August 25, 1991; the first Linux kernel release appeared on September 17, 1991. Its initial goal was a personal project for Intel 80386 computers. Combined with GNU tools and other software, Linux is used in distributions such as Ubuntu, Fedora, and Debian.

Windows, macOS, and Linux manage programs, files, and devices, but differ in vendor, compatibility, security, and software needs. Connecting an unsupported release to the internet is risky. Check device compatibility and official download sources before installing.
